t.E385.agn: In 1973 JECFA set an ADI of 0–2.5 mg/kg body weight per day, expressed as calcium disodium EDTA, and stated that no excess disodium EDTA should remain in food.
t.E385.body: Calcium disodium EDTA is very poorly absorbed from the gut: 2–4% in rats and about 2.5–5% in humans. Most of the dose (80–90% in rats) is excreted in the faeces within 24 hours.
t.E385.found.1: Canned pulses, mushrooms and artichokes (up to 250 mg/kg)
t.E385.found.2: Frozen crustaceans; canned fish, crustaceans and molluscs
t.E385.prod: Produced chemically by boiling a disodium EDTA solution with calcium carbonate.
t.E385.regx.0: ADI 0–2.5 mg/kg body weight (as calcium disodium EDTA).
t.E385.regx.1: Only in certain fat, canned, crustacean and sauce products, 75–250 mg/kg.
t.E385.summary: A binding agent known as EDTA. By binding metal ions it prevents deterioration of colour and flavour; used in canned foods, mayonnaise and sauces.
t.E385.what: An antioxidant and preservative that delays deterioration of colour and flavour by binding metal ions (chelation).
